advisory.finding: The adoption-half tests assert on the TEXT of the production source under test rather than its behavior: test_hazard_site_routes_through_the_shared_helper checks `'atomic_write' in text` and test_no_hazard_site_derives_a_temp_name_from_its_target regex-matches the source of six .py modules. These are source-grepping change-detectors — they break on a behavior-preserving refactor (renaming atomic_write, wrapping it in a local helper, reformatting the temp construction) with no observable-behavior change, and the grep target is executable source code, not a non-executable instruction artifact, so the Rule-5 structural exception does not apply.
merged_from: Five of the six changed sites have no behavioral test that drives the real production code path — the concurrency and atomicity tests call rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write DIRECTLY, and only reconcile._write_cursor is exercised through its actual function. In particular the two newly-atomic no-temp sites (janitor.reverify_entry's TOFU integrity stamp at janitor.py:305 and CriterionBank's bank upsert at completion_banking.py:511) gain atomicity in this diff, but a regression reverting either to a plain write_text would be caught only by the source-grep, not by any test that runs the function; test_banked_verdict_write_round_trips even bypasses CriterionBank entirely and writes JSON via atomic_write itself.
scenarios: A future refactor keeps atomic publishing but renames or wraps atomic_write; the grep reddens despite unchanged behavior
A site adopts an equally-correct mkstemp call inline; the 'atomic_write' grep falsely fails
